mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen from -25.0 to -23.1 over the last two weeks, indicating an emerging recovery momentum in shopping and recreation visits that should persist and push RETAIL_REC further upward over the next four weeks as consumers continue resuming pre-restriction routines.
failure_condition: If mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to the mean over the last 28 days despite the two-week uptick, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained week-on-week rise in TRANSIT mobility signals renewed use of public transit for shopping and leisure trips, which should translate into higher RETAIL_REC within two weeks as transit-dependent shoppers resume outings.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT increases by at least 1.0 point week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: If TRANSIT continues to rise for two consecutive weeks but RETAIL_REC does not increase or declines over the following two weeks, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both show simultaneous week-on-week recovery, the combined return of commuting and transit activity compounds to produce a larger rebound in RETAIL_REC than either series moving alone, because overlapping trip chains (commute plus errands) increase retail footfall disproportionately.
candidate_trigger: both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT rise in the same week relative to the prior week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -19.0 to -18.0 while TRANSIT rose from -33.7 to -32.7 in the same week
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both rise together for two or more weeks but RETAIL_REC's four-week mean does not exceed the prior four-week mean, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A plateau or decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility (from 19.9 to 19.0) signals that people are spending relatively less time confined at home, freeing discretionary time that will be redirected toward retail and recreational outings over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL declines for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL declines for two consecutive weeks but RETAIL_REC's next-two-week mean does not rise relative to the prior two-week mean, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has stabilized after a sharp drop and partial rebound (-20.6 to -11.1 to -11.0), suggesting that outdoor-recreation substitution behavior is leveling off; once PARKS volatility subsides, suppressed demand will redirect toward retail and recreation venues within the following week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS week-on-week change stays within plus or minus 2 points for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS changed by only -0.1 point between t-1w and t-0w after large prior swings
failure_condition: If PARKS stabilizes within the threshold but RETAIL_REC does not rise in the following week, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has remained deeply suppressed and essentially flat near -18 to -19 points for three consecutive weeks, indicating that workplace-closure policies remain firmly in place; this persistent restriction will continue to cap commuting-linked retail trips, keeping RETAIL_REC suppressed over the next four weeks absent a policy change.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES values were -13.0, -16.7, -19.0, -18.0 over the last four weeks, showing no sustained recovery
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES remains flat or depressed but RETAIL_REC's next-four-week mean rises above its prior four-week mean, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Weekly retail mobility series exhibit mean-reverting cyclicality; after three consecutive weeks of decline followed by one week of partial recovery, typical short-term seasonal reversion dynamics predict RETAIL_REC will tick further toward its four-week average over the coming week, producing a modest increase.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC moved from -19.6 to -24.1 to -25.0 to -23.1 across four weeks, showing a trough-and-rebound pattern typical of mean reversion
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's value one week ahead is lower than -23.1 rather than reverting upward, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous uptick in both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES in the same week, occurring under a regime of recently tightened but now loosening restrictions, indicates the start of a coordinated policy relaxation that will jointly drive a disproportionate rebound in RETAIL_REC within two weeks, exceeding what either series predicts alone.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both increase week-on-week in the same week after at least two prior weeks of decline
evidence_refs: fact:both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES improved together from t-1w to t-0w after declining in the prior two weeks
failure_condition: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both rise together in a week following prior declines, but RETAIL_REC's subsequent two-week mean does not exceed the prior two-week mean, the hypothesis is rejected.
